stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Opponents of municipal taxes on sugar-sweetened beverages have often described such levies as ______: because lower-income households devote a greater portion of their budgets to these drinks, the tax claims a larger share of their income than it does of wealthier households' income. A 2021 analysis of one city's tax complicated this charge, however. Those same households cut their purchases most sharply once the tax took effect, and so stood to gain the most from the resulting drop in diabetes risk.
explanation: The colon tells you the blank is defined by what follows it. The opponents' complaint is that the tax takes a larger share of income from poorer households than from wealthier ones. That is exactly what "regressive" means: a tax whose burden falls proportionally harder on people with less income. The 2021 finding pushes back on the charge by pointing to who benefits. It doesn't redefine the charge, so the blank still has to name the income-share complaint.

A.why: You chose a criticism that people really do make of soda taxes: that the government is overriding personal choices. You matched the topic, not this sentence. The colon spells out the complaint, and it is about how much of each household's income the tax takes. It says nothing about restricting freedom of choice.

C.why: You noticed that the burden falls on poorer households and picked a word with roughly the right negative tone. But "punitive" means meant to punish. The opponents in the passage describe how the cost is distributed. They never claim the tax was designed to punish anyone, so this word claims more than the text supports.

D.why: You may have read ahead to the reduced purchases and taken "prohibitive" to describe them. A prohibitive cost is high enough to stop people from buying at all. The opponents' complaint only makes sense if households keep buying and keep paying the tax, since that is how it 'claims a larger share' of their income. The word clashes with the definition after the colon.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Clay can hold a surprising quantity of water: in some deposits, the open space between particles exceeds 40 percent of the sediment's total volume, far more than in many sandstones. Yet clay layers make notoriously poor aquifers. Because those spaces are minute and only weakly connected to one another, clay is nearly ______, transmitting water so slowly that a well drilled into it may yield almost nothing for years.
explanation: The "because" clause gives you the logic. The spaces in clay are tiny and poorly connected, so water barely moves through it, and a well yields almost nothing. The blank has to mean 'does not let water pass through.' That is "impermeable." The passage separates two properties. Clay has plenty of space for water (it is highly porous) but almost no ability to move it (it is nearly impermeable). The answer must name the second property without denying the first.

A.why: This is the trap that survives the key insight. You correctly worked out that clay blocks the flow of water, then reached for the familiar word that seems to say so. But "nonporous" means having no open spaces, and the first sentence says clay's open space can be more than 40 percent of its volume. Clay is porous. What it lacks is permeability.

B.why: You picked a word that sounds like it is about water and solids. "Insoluble" means 'does not dissolve.' Whether clay dissolves has nothing to do with how slowly water moves through it, and that is the property the sentence describes.

D.why: You may have connected 'yields almost nothing' to dryness. "Desiccated" means thoroughly dried out, but the passage stresses that clay holds a large quantity of water. The well fails because the water can't flow out, not because there is none.
